clue.text: Hot winter clothing master's left for pets

indicators.note: the master has left, so the abbreviation for master walks out of the clothing word

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
muffs keep hands or ears warm in winter
M is a standard abbreviation for master

explanation.surface: A warmly dressed owner leaves the house, leaving coats and muffs behind for the household animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like animals, but here it is a plural noun for fits of sulking: in a pet, in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the older sense is a fit of peevish sulking, the same as a huff, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Prepared with craft broken down in harbour

indicators.note: a broken word has its letters smashed apart and set in a new order
in places the jumbled letters within the word for harbour

blocks.note: a haven is a harbour
the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat prepared with care has broken down inside the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat beside the harbour; it means handicraft skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-woven cloth is made on a hand loom, a product of skilled handicraft rather than a machine.

clue.text: Powerful person in government, Angela Merkel, for instance

definitions.text: Powerful person in government, Angela Merkel, for instance

blocks.note: surface reading: a senior official in a cabinet with responsibility for diplomacy
setter's reading: to a British reader she is a government minister who happens to come from abroad

explanation.walkthrough: Merkel was German Chancellor, never her country's diplomatic chief; the clue reads the title literally as a minister from another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, a government head from Germany is a minister who is foreign to British readers.

clue.text: Craps game leads to slippery slope

indicators.note: a game leg is a lame or injured one, so the letters are damaged into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gambling at dice is the start of a slippery slope towards ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like it describes craps, but it is the anagram signal; 'slippery slope' is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarp is a steep bank or escarpment, the kind of slope one might slide down.

clue.text: Those managing to free back, releasing corset

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for free from right to left
releasing the corset lets its letters loosen and fall into a new order

blocks.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests
the letters of the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to free their back from a tight corset, a little Victorian comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors manage a company's affairs, so they are the people managing it.

clue.text: Separate daughter and son between two islands

indicators.note: between puts the letter for son in the gap, with an island on each side

blocks.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
I is the abbreviation for island, and Crete is a Greek island
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family split up, with the daughter and son living on two different islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct, existing apart from others, so it is the adjective separate.

clue.text: Playing in drab strip

indicators.note: playing with something moves it about, so the letters are toyed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A team playing in a dull, drab football strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a team kit; it means a narrow length of ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A riband is an old word for a ribbon, a narrow strip of cloth often worn as a decoration.

clue.text: Applaud entertaining maiden and overthrow suppression

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means having them inside, so a letter goes within

blocks.note: to clap is to applaud
M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over
to down an opponent is to overthrow them

explanation.surface: Cheering a young woman while a regime is toppled, all part of a crackdown on dissent.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a severe official crackdown, the suppression of an activity.

clue.text: Test confidence after losing leader, greatest upset before one country

indicators.note: losing its leader means the first letter is dropped from the word for confidence
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads the other way

blocks.note: morale is a group's confidence
max is short for maximum, the greatest
I is the Roman numeral one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A country loses confidence after its leader departs, and the strongest suffer an upset.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral examination is a spoken test, such as a viva, so it is a kind of test.

clue.text: Gowns, sort to be carried by ship

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the vessel, so one word goes within

blocks.note: SS stands for steamship
ilk means sort or kind

explanation.surface: Fine dresses, of a certain sort, being shipped overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, senior barristers (King's Counsel) wear silk gowns, and are said to take silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Silks are the silk gowns worn by senior barristers, and dresses of silk generally.

clue.text: Some Frenchmen contracted ordinary Poles

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, so the word for ordinary loses its final letter

blocks.note: normal means ordinary
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A report of French workers signing up an ordinary pair of Polish labourers on contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to be people from Poland; it is the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Normans are the people of Normandy in northern France, so they are some of the French.

clue.text: Scrap housing commercial, one that bores

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a scrap is a fight, a brawl
a commercial is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out around a television advert, and the advert is dismissed as one that bores viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One that bores' reads as a tedious person or advert, but it is a tool that drills holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool used to pierce holes in wood, so it is a boring tool.

clue.text: Youths showing cheek through separating cat and fish

indicators.note: separating places the word for through in the gap between the two creatures

blocks.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip
per means through or by means of
snappers are a family of fish; the plural follows the plural youths

explanation.surface: Cheeky lads come between a cat and the fish it is stalking.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is not an animal but the old naval whip, the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippersnappers are impudent young people, upstarts who show cheek to their elders.

clue.text: Feud tortured vet at end

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-running quarrel ends with a veterinarian being tortured, a grim little revenge story.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter quarrel or blood feud between families or people.

clue.text: Report of how investigator might describe job application targeted at women

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a private detective tails people, describing the work in two words

explanation.surface: A private detective's account of a job application aimed at female candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' suggests a job form but means something applied to the face; a private eye says what the job is.
explanation.definitionFit: This make-up is applied to the eyelids and marketed mainly to women, so it is a cosmetic application.

clue.text: Working inside, modelled a composition

indicators.note: inside places the word for working within the word for modelled

blocks.note: an artist's model sat for the painter
a machine that is on is working
taken as written

explanation.surface: A model working indoors posed for a picture, a composition in paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' leans towards painting with the model, but it is a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical work for one or a few instruments, so it is a composition.

clue.text: Share mental wrangling about destiny

indicators.note: wrangling is arguing and twisting, so the letters are tussled into a new order
about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the next word

blocks.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Heirs argue madly about fate and their share of the inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a portion allocated to someone, an allocated share of something.

clue.text: Very old creature is restful

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
O is a standard abbreviation for old
a thing can be any creature, as in poor thing

explanation.surface: An ancient animal, such as a tortoise, is very calm and restful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soothing calms and relaxes you, so it is restful in its effect.

clue.text: Accomplished celebrity cook, Nigella's beginning to make comeback

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is just its first letter
coming back means travelling the other way, so the joined letters run right to left

blocks.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook
Nigella Lawson is another TV cook; only her initial is used

explanation.surface: A skilled TV cook is upstaged as Nigella starts a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith and Nigella Lawson are two of Britain's best-known television cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to do it perfectly, so nailed means accomplished successfully.

clue.text: Departs private hospital, sick and declining

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
one's own is private to oneself
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A patient leaves a private hospital still sick and getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downhill is an idiom for getting worse, so the adjective means deteriorating or declining.

clue.text: Granny oddly hid animated film epic

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the letters in odd positions: first, third and fifth
animated means set in lively motion, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word
the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grandma strangely hid from a cartoon blockbuster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated film' looks like a cartoon, but 'animated' is the anagram signal and the film is live action.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandhi is Richard Attenborough's 1982 Oscar-winning biopic, a long epic film.

clue.text: In half-light at ten, Dante receives help on lines

indicators.note: in says the solution lies within the following words
the phrase receives the solution, holding it inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of half through to just before the last letter of Dante

explanation.surface: In the dusk at ten o'clock, Dante gets help with his verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests poetry with Dante; it means airlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin crew member assists passengers on airline flights, so is help on airlines.

clue.text: Puts on designs after sex-change

indicators.note: a sex change swaps the letter for male for the letter for female

blocks.note: to make something is to design and produce it

explanation.surface: Someone tries on new outfits after transitioning.
explanation.walkthrough: M for male becomes F for female.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an accent or illness is to fake it, pretending to have it.

clue.text: Relative half-chance, that is to be taken in

indicators.note: half keeps only part of the word, here its back three letters
being taken in means going inside, so a short abbreviation enters the kept letters

blocks.note: the second half of the six-letter word
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A relative has half a chance of being taken in, by a con perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of a sibling, so she is a family member.

clue.text: Eating time, one following jay finished insect

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so the letter for time goes inside

blocks.note: the letter K comes after J in the alphabet, and its name is spelt out
T is the abbreviation for time
to have done something is to have finished it

explanation.surface: A jay, a bird, finishes eating an insect it has caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jay' looks like the bird but is the letter J spelt out; the one following it in the alphabet is K.
explanation.definitionFit: A katydid is a North American bush cricket, a grasshopper-like insect named for its call.

clue.text: After reorganisation, site invites in recording company to make inventory

indicators.note: once reorganised, the letters stand in a different order
inviting someone in brings them inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged
EMI is a well-known British record label

explanation.surface: After a shake-up, a website brings in a record label to catalogue its stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one, which is what making an inventory involves.

clue.text: Spread out well to protect a wall's perimeter

indicators.note: protecting surrounds and shelters, so one word wraps around the others
the perimeter of a word is only its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a spring is a natural well of water
taken as written
only the outside letters of wall are kept

explanation.surface: Water from a spring is spreading across the ground, so a wall is built around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sprawling extends untidily over a wide area, so it is spread out.

clue.text: Surrealist showing birds back to front

indicators.note: one end of the word swaps place, the front letter going round to the back

blocks.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: A surrealist painting of birds turned back to front, the sort of thing Magritte might do.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German painter, a founder of Dada and Surrealism.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was one of the leading Surrealist painters, so he is an example of a Surrealist.
